newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cruise liner grounded in Arctic sightly damaged.
newsitem.headline: Cruise liner grounded in Arctic sightly damaged.

text.p: A Bahamian-registered cruise liner that ran aground off an Arctic island has only minor damage and could continue its voyage once freed, a tour company said on Monday.

A spokesman for Hapag-Lloyd AG in Hamburg said the Hanseatic, the same boat that ran into a sandbank in the Canadian Arctic a year ago, was inspected by divers after running aground off the island of Spitzbergen, Norway on Sunday.
They found no leaks and only minor damage to the 9,000-deadweight-tonne cruise ship, the spokesman said. He said the 145 passengers on the luxury tour, mostly Germans, were in good spirits.
Two Norwegian coast guard ships were en route to the vessel and would try to pull it free at high tide on Monday evening, the spokesman said.
The Hanseatic also ran aground last August. The same captain hit a sandbank on a voyage in northwest Canada, ending the boat's tour through the Arctic for the 268 people on board.
Many of the passengers were transferred to an icebreaker after waiting for a week on the stranded ship.
In Oslo, the Norwegian Pollution Directorate and the coast guard planned to decide later if it was necessary to unload the ship's fuel before trying to pull the vessel free.
The Hanseatic ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off the north coast of Spitzbergen. No one was hurt and there was only slight damage to the hull at midships, rescue officials said.
The ship was carrying 480 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, 35 tonnes of diesel and 10 tonnes of gasoline.
All passengers and crew were still aboard the liner, which had been on its way from Norway to Iceland.
A Swedish passenger ship, Origo, unsuccessfully tried to pull the Hanseatic free and was waiting alongside.
